title: Curly Message Format conformance fixture file
description: One file of the conformance set: cases pinning one section of the specification at one conformance level. README.md in this package states what each field means.

format.description: The versioned identifier of the format the file targets.

level.description: The conformance level (section 2) that requires every case in the file.

section.description: The section of SPEC.md the file pins; a case may name a more specific one.
A heading number of SPEC.md: a section ("7"), a subsection ("9.2") or an appendix entry ("A.4").

identifier.description: Unique across the whole set: the file's group, a slash, and a slug.

concrete.description: A resolution written out: its inputs and what they must produce.

message.description: The message, usually text. Any other JSON value is a message a host wrote as something else (section 4); the undefined tag is a message the caller did not supply (section 10).

payload.description: The payload (section 3). Entries hold values, wrappers (section 4.1) or tagged values.

props.description: The caller's formatting properties, grouped by modifier name (section 11.2).

messageId.description: The message's id (section 4), spelled out because a case's own `id` names the case. Any JSON value: no step of resolution reads it, and reports name it (section 14.3).

modifiers.description: Host-defined modifiers to register (section 11.3), each the name of a behaviour from the catalogue.

defaults.description: The implementation-configured defaults: the bottom formatting layer of section 11.2, grouped by modifier name.

generated.description: A case the runner builds from the limits the adapter declares (section 13); the README states each construction.

description.description: One sentence naming what the case pins, for the failure it would print.

output.description: The text the resolution must produce.

format.description: For a locale-dependent output: the formatting request whose result on the running host is the text the resolution must produce. The message is then the placeholder alone.

reports.description: The reports the resolution must emit, in the order it emits them. Omitted, none are expected.

options.description: The options the request is constructed with: the properties the facility reads, as the layers of section 11.2 compose them and the modifier pins them, without the format's own ratio and format, which the input already reflects.

input.description: What the request formats: a number for NumberFormat, milliseconds since the epoch for DateTimeFormat, a [value, unit] pair for RelativeTimeFormat.

id.description: The id the report must name, where the adapter's reports carry one. Text, and compared as written: tagged values (see the package README) are read on a case's inputs and not in its expectations, so a case whose id is not text leaves this out and the id goes unobserved.
